output.summary: The architectural entry point is the shared canvas controller and its exact bindings to immutable diagram revisions. Browser editing, agent commands, generated alternatives, and change proposals converge on this core. Durable publication, reusable source contexts, and evaluations form distinct supporting boundaries. Diagram-edit generation and proposal workflows have separate orchestration; chat-derived evaluations explicitly delegate reruns and cancellation back to chat.

points.title: Canvas Commands and History
points.rationale: MappingDocumentController coordinates versioned semantic mutations for browser sessions and isolated proposals. CanvasHistoryService owns checkpoints, branching, named views, transfers, and restoration. Each checkpoint binds exact immutable diagram revisions while separating composition from personal view state. Together with diagram revisions, this is the central entry point for understanding the system.

relationships.label: Issues edits and binds exact diagram revisions
Uses checkpoint encoding for incremental persistence
Validates and retains diagram context bindings

points.title: Immutable Diagram Revisions
points.rationale: Diagram content, parser-derived nodes, logical node continuity, source mappings, and revision ancestry meet here. Domain operations validate edits and issue immutable revisions; the runtime registry retains their identities. Canvas placements reference this content, allowing composition changes without creating content revisions and history restoration without substituting newer diagrams.

points.title: Checkpoint and Catalog Persistence
points.rationale: Immutable diagram and checkpoint records sit behind separate mutable workspace and publication boundaries. Browser autosave submits incremental batches with revision guards and durable retry receipts. Catalog publication exposes saved checkpoints after their backing records exist, and proposal acceptance publishes all affected canvas heads and its receipt together.

relationships.label: Persists and restores validated immutable revisions
Encodes histories and publishes exact checkpoint bindings

points.title: Interactive Canvas Runtime
points.rationale: CanvasWorkspace owns document-session lifetimes, and CanvasSession exposes separate reactive stores for semantic state and presentation. The tldraw adapter owns live geometry and native undo navigation, commits settled gestures through the controller, and restores archived semantic checkpoints. Shape projection and routing connect domain state to interactive rendering.

relationships.label: Owns controllers and commits settled gestures
Connects workspace changes to incremental autosave
Registers browser canvases and handles dispatched commands
Hosts conversations bound to the active canvas

points.title: Live Canvas Agent API
points.rationale: AgentDiagrammingSessionService exposes canvas operations through HTTP-backed MCP tools and a constrained JavaScript executor. Its command bridge reaches the owning browser or routes proposal operations to ChangeSessionService. LiveCanvasService separately binds selection streams to workspace, document, and epoch identities. Compact anchors, version checks, and retry receipts preserve identity across these boundaries.

relationships.label: Dispatches commands to the owning browser
Uses shared semantic operations and state projections
Starts and monitors diagram edits and batches
Routes proposal-scoped reads and mutations
Exposes saved and diagram-bound context operations

points.title: Reusable Agent Contexts
points.rationale: AgentContext represents a validated, hash-addressed conversation and source-evidence snapshot for independent model sessions. The library adds durable discovery, forks, comments, and lineage. Source adapters preserve exact Git content or immutable snapshots, while diagram-bound contexts record their originating revision and detect changes to captured evidence.

relationships.label: Compiles context from diagram source evidence
Captures source ranges through corpus access
Stores captured source content as immutable records

points.title: Validated Diagram Edit Pipeline
points.rationale: DiagramEditService pins input revisions and prepares creation, extension, scoped replacement, or variants. Generator ports and validated submission precede domain revision issuance. DiagramBatchService stages results against one snapshot before installation. Application acknowledgement has its own state, allowing uncertain persistence responses to retry the prepared operation without regenerating content.

relationships.label: Validates submissions and issues content revisions
Resolves captured context to seed generation
Installs prepared revisions through versioned canvas ports

points.title: Agent Chat Orchestration
points.rationale: AgentChatService manages persisted conversations, native thread resume, streaming events, and turn-bound tools through a Codex app-server connection. Generated alternatives receive isolated controllers through GenerationCanvasBridge. Chat publishes candidate progress and results to the evaluation observer and retains the executor used when evaluations request chat-derived reruns or cancellation.

relationships.label: Invokes tools bound to the current conversation turn
Owns isolated controllers for generated alternatives
Loads saved contexts for independent child conversations
Reports candidate lifecycle and results through the evaluation observer

points.title: Git Change Proposals
points.rationale: ChangeSessionService captures repository-scoped baselines and Git hunks, edits isolated proposals, and accepts ready results against unchanged originals. DiffSessionWorkflowService runs analysis and materialization through the generic validated step runner, also used by file compaction. That runner belongs here as a demonstrated proposal dependency. Push ingestion pins commit endpoints and deduplicates events before launching this workflow.

relationships.label: Edits isolated proposals with shared controllers
Persists proposal records and atomically publishes accepted canvases
Supplies canvas tools for proposal materialization

points.title: Generation Evaluation Workbench
points.rationale: Evaluation runs freeze prompts, contexts, canvas inputs, and output provenance. Comparisons capture independent checkpoints; experiments organize conditions and samples; judgements retain typed assessments. Chat-derived runs observe candidate results and delegate reruns and cancellation to AgentChatService. Other evaluations use their own runtime, sharing the Pi session adapter with diagram editing. Completed outputs can be promoted through catalog publication.

relationships.label: Delegates chat-derived reruns and cancellation to the retained executor
Pins and resolves reusable evaluation inputs
Reads saved checkpoints and publishes promoted outputs
Captures versioned proposal results as frozen outputs
Retains exact checkpoint histories for comparisons

points.title: Source Evidence and Navigation
points.rationale: Source access resolves explicit diagram repository bindings, including multiple repositories within one project. Node mappings become source-range references; corpus providers enforce repository-relative access. Optional language-service sessions resolve definitions against verified file hashes. This boundary connects diagram semantics to inspectable backing code and reusable source evidence.

relationships.label: Resolves diagram bindings and mapped node evidence
Loads published revisions and source bindings

points.title: Runtime Composition and Lifetime
points.rationale: The composition roots choose concrete adapters and inject application services. Vite configuration controls HTTP writes, model execution, and language services; the server adapter mounts transports, translates errors, and disposes resources on shutdown. This point explains assembly and lifetime, handing service behavior off to the dedicated feature points.

relationships.label: Constructs and injects persistence adapters
Assembles command bridges and attaches live transports
Constructs the chat connection and owns shutdown
Wires push ingestion and proposal execution
Connects evaluation observation, replay, and cancellation callbacks
Configures corpus access and optional language services

points.title: Static Architecture Analysis
points.rationale: A separate TypeScript pipeline extracts containment, references, calls, ownership, and dependencies with evidence provenance. It supports incremental analysis, derived partitions and metrics, and deterministic artifacts. Source-join helpers match pinned diagram leaf ranges to source entities. The inspected CLI invokes analysis independently; the join helpers do not establish integration with the interactive canvas.

relationships.label: Provides helpers joining pinned diagram leaves to source entities

limitations: The requested complete source-body read was not achieved. The 1,044-file inventory received a broad survey, followed by substantive implementation and test inspection of the files listed in reviewedPaths. Several large listed files were inspected selectively; declaration-only surveys and search hits are not counted there as substantive reviews.

Most test bodies, peripheral UI components and styles, browser and performance harnesses, migration and evaluation scripts, the projection-3d prototype, and Python parser tooling remain uninspected beyond short excerpts or declarations. Parser and static-analysis internals received partial implementation review.

The generic workflow runner is shared with file compaction. Its placement with change proposals identifies a demonstrated consumer, not exclusive ownership. Diagram editing and evaluations share the Pi session adapter without a demonstrated evaluation-to-diagram-edit pipeline call.
Source-join helpers have inspected definitions and test callers, but no interactive-backend integration was established. Their diagram relationship is therefore marked related.

The index excludes corpus data, investigations, artifacts, generated stores/builds, vendor dependencies, node_modules, documentation except the root README, binaries/assets, and lockfiles. No live repository, external sources, or existing diagrams were consulted, and no application or tests were executed.
